policy: ADR-026 D8. Each case pins one couple-local dayKey (yyyymmdd) to its Umm al-Qura Hijri date and to the EXACT set of seasonal windows open on it. Every window carries both sides of both edges, so an off-by-one at any boundary reddens. Two properties are load-bearing and deliberate: (a) the 1448 Ramadan pair sits ~11 Gregorian days earlier than the 1447 pair, so any 'Gregorian month mistaken for a Hijri month' bug fails; (b) Ramadan 1447 is 30 days while Ramadan 1448 is 29, so an implementation that hardcodes a month length instead of testing month === 9 fails. Hijri values were verified against Node 20 full-ICU (calendar islamic-umalqura) when ADR-026 was written; this file is therefore also the ICU-data drift guard — if a future ICU revision moves an Umm al-Qura date, this suite goes red instead of the product quietly shifting. Unlike day-key-parity.json this fixture has NO Dart side by design (ADR-026 D7): the client never computes a selection.

cases.note: ramadan exit edge, inside — a 30-day Ramadan
ramadan exit outside AND eid_fitr entry inside, same day
new_year across the Gregorian year boundary (Jan 1)
ramadan 1448 entry edge, inside — ~11 Gregorian days earlier than 1447
ramadan 1448 exit edge, inside — a 29-day Ramadan
ramadan 1448 exit outside AND eid_fitr entry inside
